capabilities.local_comparison: Compare two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change. Measures local plan/endpoint differences; does not establish closed-loop settling or causal attribution. Requires a saved effective horizon matching the authorized horizon.
capabilities.prediction_braking: At one saved projected state, compare recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences. Cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same result; cannot identify the dominant settling cause.

recommendations.rationale: The final saved projected state (update 34) has an effective horizon of 1 control interval, matching the authorized 0.01 s horizon, so a local_comparison with exactly one adopted weight change is scope-permissible; however it measures only local plan/endpoint differences and cannot establish closed-loop settling or attribute the residual tip speed, so it is deferred pending adoption in a later phase.

A prediction_braking comparison at the final saved projected state over the fixed 0.01 s horizon can measure local endpoint speed/position differences between recorded input and an instantaneous braking-box input, but cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, effective-horizon truncation, or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same local endpoint; deferred pending adoption.

Complete coverage reads of the earlier sampled backend motion and one-step predictions (updates 0–26) are recommended before any check, to confirm whether the residual tip speed develops only within the final window; deferred to a later phase.

attribution.reason: Recorded recipe weights (tracking 1.0; velocity 1e-4; terminal_velocity 1e-4; tension 1e-4) are raw magnitudes with no retained cost-term contributions, so whether the terminal-velocity term governs the residual speed is not observable; the recorded one-step endpoint differences (tip differences ~1e-3–5e-3 m, velocity vector differences ~0.10–0.12 m/s) are compatible with several hypotheses.

Selections are recorded (initialization_selected=29, noninitialization_selected=6) with policy stop reasons such as relative_seed_improvement and budget_best_feasible, but the full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces required to separate seed/initialization choice from objective weighting are not retained.

The per-update effective horizon shrinks to a single 0.01 s control interval by update 34 versus the configured 10; a one-interval problem limits braking lookahead and is consistent with residual tip speed, but the retained local checks cannot establish it as the dominant settling cause.

The retained one-step comparisons (projected GVS prediction versus full serial-backend endpoint) show only small tip/velocity differences and are explicitly scoped as recorded projected states, not full backend-state error, so they do not separate model mismatch from weighting, seed, or horizon effects.

facts.statement: The retained execution reports reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m≈0.00764 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance, while sampled_settling_passed=false with late_max_error_m≈0.0581 m and late_max_speed_m_s≈1.581 m/s against the settling limits 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s over a 0.05 s window.

All 35 retained control updates are recorded as deadline misses (deadline_misses=35) with mean_update_s≈17.08 s against a 0.01 s control period; stopping counts are 34 User_Requested_Stop and 1 Solve_Succeeded.
Per-update effective horizon decreases across the final window: 8 (update 27), 6 (29), 5 (30), 4 (31), 3 (32), 2 (33), 1 (34) control intervals, versus a configured horizon of 10.

In the sampled final window (0.30–0.35 s) the tip error falls toward the reach tolerance (late_motion[5].error_m≈0.00764 m) while measured tip speed stays elevated (0.862 m/s at t=0.30, 1.477 m/s at t=0.32, and terminal_speed_m_s≈0.635 m/s at t=0.35).

request_content.question: Given that the single retained execution reports terminal reach success (reach_passed=true; terminal_error_m≈0.00764 m within the 0.01 m reach tolerance) while sampled settling fails (sampled_settling_passed=false; late_max_speed_m_s≈1.581 and late_max_error_m≈0.058 against settling limits speed 0.02 m/s and position 0.01 m over a 0.05 s window), and all 35 retained control updates missed their DeadlineMissed horizons with mean_update_s≈17.08 s against a 0.01 s control period: which candidate local mechanisms are actually distinguishable using the retained per-update records (saved projected states, applied and requested tensions, one-step predictions, plan-selection iterations, effective horizon, solver status, and the sampled backend-motion view), and specifically — at the final saved projected states — can a bounded local_comparison of one adopted weight change, or a prediction_braking comparison of recorded input versus instantaneous braking-box input, separate objective weighting, seed/initialization selection, horizon truncation, or backend-model mismatch, or do these predict the same local result and leave the residual tip motion (speed vs position) unattributed? This is an open question; no dominant settling cause is assumed.
scope: Retained-evidence reads of the complete saved-record inventories for this execution (35 records each): source.saved_projected_states (/measured_initial_state), source.one_step_predictions (/one_step_prediction), source.applied_tensions (/actual_tension_n), source.plan_selection (/optimization_selected_iteration), source.solver_status (/optimization_raw_status), source.controller_horizon (/effective_horizon), plus the derived motion/plans/prediction views and the retained source.force_limits channel list.
The recovered common summary and inventory handoff (artifact e87b0e85...) already transferred to this design context, including the settling criteria, recipe weights, and outcome flags.

Explicitly authorized saved-state numerical work only: prediction_braking at one saved projected state over the fixed short bounded horizon, and local_comparison of two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change, using the host-supplied saved-state grant (horizon_s 0.01, integration_step_s 0.002, implicit_euler, model.gvs@1.0.0). These measure only local plan/endpoint differences at a saved state.

Excluded: any production configuration change, backend re-execution, closed-loop counterfactual replay, or causal-attribution claim; reconstruction of non-retained control_snapshots.json (full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces); any inference from a sampled view or a failed raw-gzip read that a signal is absent.

Distinguish availability states explicitly: not_displayed (present but not yet shown), not_read in this design context, queried with stated coverage, not_retained (control_snapshots.json), and retained_unavailable via a named capability.
stopping_conditions: All 35 retained records for each consulted signal are read once, or the read/turn allowance is exhausted, with coverage recorded per signal.
Any candidate local check is abandoned if it requires non-retained artifacts (full warm plans, optimizer iteration traces) or a closed-loop replay that the available capabilities do not provide.
